newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares slip as Wolford takes a knock.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares slip as Wolford takes a knock.

text.p: Austria's blue-chip ATX index slipped 0.67 percent on Thursday as hosiery maker Wolford dropped six percent after a presentation to U.S. investors stoked rumours that 1996/97 profits may disappoint.
The ATX closed 8.24 points down at 1,215.24 with eight issues higher and 13 lower.
Wolford shares tumbled 160 schillings, or nine percent, before recovering some composure to end 90 down at 1,320.
Behind the weakness were rumours that high expansion costs in the United States and the Far East may weigh on earnings in the 1996/97 financial year, Vienna traders said.
"It seems the rumours started with a Wolford presentation in the United States on Wednesday," one local dealer said.
A Wolford spokesman rejected the talk as baseless.
"The rumours are absolutely without foundation. We are completely on target. Nothing has changed since our half-year news conference (in December)," the spokesman said.
International analysts also dismissed the speculation.
"If anyone sold on the back of a profit warning for the current year they did not do their homework. Both sides say the conference call with U.S. clients was very positive," said one.
In the six months to October 31, 1996 Wolford reported a nine percent rise in net profit and forecast full-year sales of 1.7 billion schillings, surpassing the previous year's 1.475 billion record.
NatWest analyst David Abraham noted that Wolford was sticking to its earnings per share forecast of 39-42 schillings for the current year.
In otherwise uneventful trade, the ATX index shifted to a 1,210-1,220 points range.

"Its going to take news from outside the market to move the ATX index out of this range," said a trader, noting that final 1996 company results due for release next week had already been well flagged.

Among the top gainers were Radex-Heraklith, still buoyed by strong 1996 earnings issued on Wednesday with a bullish forecast for 1997, and carton board maker Mayr-Melnhof, which has said it expects the acquisition of a Reynolds packaging plant to boost sales.
April ATX futures fell 9.5 points to 1,218.5. The board-based Vienna share index finished 2.45 points down at 456.13.
The Vienna stock market will be closed on Friday and Monday. -- Janet McBride, Vienna newsroom +43-1 531 12 254
